title: Ki Tisa: show me thy glory (Exodus 33:18–23)
hook: Moses asks to see God, and sees only from behind, from a cleft in the rock

segments.voice: Yesterday, v'shamru: even the holy building stops for Shabbat. Your line was even the temple rests. What did you put down? Day three hundred sixty-six.

Between yesterday's verses and today's, the worst thing has happened. While Moses was on the mountain, the people made a golden calf. Moses came down, saw them dancing, and broke the tablets of stone. Then came the long climb back: pleading for the people, pitching a tent outside the camp, speaking with God face to face, the text says, as a man speaks to his friend. And now, after all of it, Moses asks for one more thing. The boldest request anyone makes in the whole Torah. He wants to see God.
screen: `THE GOLDEN CALF.` → `THE TABLETS BROKEN.` → `ONE MORE REQUEST: SHOW ME.`

segments.voice: In the JPS 1917 translation, it's one short line: "Show me, I pray Thee, Thy glory." God's answer comes in layers. First, a yes: I will make all My goodness pass before you, and call out My name. Then a no: you cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live. Then a way through. There's a place by Me, God says, stand on the rock. I'll put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand while I pass by. And then: "I will take away My hand, and thou shalt see My back; but My face shall not be seen." So Moses, closest of all people to God, sees only from behind. What does that mean? The Torah doesn't explain, and Jewish readers have never agreed. The Talmud, in Berakhot, says God showed Moses the knot of the tefillin at the back of the head: a picture, not a portrait. Maimonides says the face means God's essence, which no mind can grasp, and the back means God's ways in the world, which can be learned. And many readers have heard something quieter in it. In life, you rarely see God coming. You see where God has been. Only looking back, at a hard year, a rescue, a meeting that changed everything, does a person sometimes say: there. That was it. Moses doesn't get the face. He gets a rock to stand on, a hand over his eyes, and the view from behind.
screen: `SHOW ME THY GLORY.` · `NO ONE SEES MY FACE AND LIVES.` · `A CLEFT IN THE ROCK, A HAND.` · `SEEN ONLY FROM BEHIND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look back. Settle, and breathe. Think of a time, months or years ago, that was hard while you were in it. Don't relive the worst of it. Just walk forward from there in your mind, slowly, to now. Who showed up? What held? What turned out differently than you feared? Notice anything that looks, from here, like a hand over the cleft in the rock. If you pray, you can say thank you for it. If you don't, just let yourself see it. The bell holds the time.
Ki Tisa. The portion of the golden calf, the broken tablets, and Moses in the cleft of the rock, seeing God only from behind.
Your line: seen only from behind. Tonight, look back over today and name one moment that looks better from here. Day three hundred sixty-six.

screen: `DAY 366 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: KI TISA: THE THIRTEEN ATTRIBUTES.`

howItsDone: This passage, Exodus 33:12–34:26, is also the Torah reading for the Shabbat during Passover and Sukkot, so many Jews hear Moses' request several times a year.

fork.setup: you're Moses. you've just pleaded the people back from the golden calf. you have God's ear. what do you ask for?
options: to be released from leading them.
fork.reveal: show me, I pray Thee, Thy glory. God puts him in a cleft of the rock, covers him with a hand, and lets him see only from behind.

original.note: Hebrew: show me, please, Your glory, Moses' request in Exodus 33:18.

trapdoor: what you thought: Moses gets a glimpse of God.
what it means: Moses is refused the face, sheltered in a rock, and shown only the back, as God passes by.
what a scholar hears: Berakhot 7a reads the back as the knot of the tefillin; Maimonides (Guide 1:54) reads it as God's ways, knowable, against God's essence, which is not.

notes: Exodus 33:18 and 33:23 quoted from JPS 1917; confirm wording, including 'I will take away My hand'.
The golden calf (Exodus 32) is summarized in the hook since the outline goes straight from 31 to 33; a Keeper may want the calf to have its own day.
'Face to face, as a man speaks to his friend' (33:11) is paraphrased in the hook.
Berakhot 7a (knot of the tefillin) and Maimonides, Guide 1:54 (back = God's ways/attributes of action): confirm.
The 'you see where God has been' reading is offered as what 'many readers' hear, not as a classical source.
howItsDone: Exodus 33:12–34:26 is read on Shabbat Chol HaMoed of Passover and Sukkot; confirm.
